To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
non-obstructive LM CAD is frequently detected by CCTA and strongly associated with future adverse events in women.
nonobstructive left main (LM, or left main coronary artery) plaque was associated with increased risk of adverse events in women, but not in men.
nonobstructive left main coronary artery disease is associated with adverse events and this is more pronounced in women than men.

a novel approach to risk stratification of patients with nonobstructured left main coronary artery disease (LMCAD), using the results of coronary computed tomography angiography (CTA).
the prognostic implications of nonobstructed left main coronary disease.
sex-specific differences in the prognostic value of nonobstructed left main coronary artery disease (LM CAD) in patients with suspected or known coronary artery disease ( CAD).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sex specific prognostic significance is not yet established.
nonobstructive left main disease is an independent predictor of adverse cardiovascular events in women, but not men.

the presence of non-obstructive LM CAD on CTA is associated with worse outcomes than normal coronary artery anatomy, particularly in women, but the presence of non- obstructive LM CAD does not appear to have worse outcomes than non-obstructive CAD at other locations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
women with non-obstructive LM CAD are at high risk.
women with nonobstrictive LM plaque have worse prognosis than men with non-obstructive LM plaque.
nonobstructive left main disease is more prevalent in women than men and is associated with increased mortality in women but not men.
The main takeaway from our work is that

women with nonobstrictive (1% - 49%) left main disease on CTA should be considered for aggressive risk modification strategies and follow-up, and that this is a group that warrants more research to better understand the underlying biology and pathophysiology.

women with nonobstrictive LM plaque are at higher risk of future cardiac events compared with men.
